html:
Yoweri Museveni has been president of Uganda since January 1986, when his guerrilla army took Kampala at the end of the Bush War.

He restored order after years of terror, rebuilt the economy with market reforms and won praise for a frank campaign against HIV. He let the old kingdoms return as cultural institutions in 1993. His army helped the Rwandan Patriotic Front and later fought in Congo.

For years parties were restricted under his no-party Movement system. Term limits were removed in 2005 and the age limit in 2017, and elections have been marred by violence against opponents. In the north, his army fought the Lord's Resistance Army for two decades. He is one of the longest-serving rulers in Africa, in Uganda.
sum: Yoweri Museveni has been president of Uganda since January 1986, when his guerrilla army took Kampala at the end of the Bush War.
